items.claim: Paint ignores a region's own `chromeId` while the hit test honors it
Escape returns to a default tool the active mode bars
Overlapping point regions ranked by world distance, not screen distance
Annulus paint and `minBandPx` floor assume the cutout is centered on (cx, cy), while the hit test uses its real position
items.note: (floor, which hit and paint share) and 1cbb8a8f49 (paint)

items.claim: Annulus petals wind against each other, leaving corner holes under nonzero fill and drawing chords across the band with a stroke
items.note: It is one rewrite with the finding above: the fill is now the ring split into disjoint pieces around the real cutout, and the stroke is a separate command tracing only the ring's outline

items.claim: A `KeyState` attached to two targets loses its window-blur release when either detaches
items.note: The detach's `release()` still clears keys the other attachment holds; the `attach` doc promises "the detach, which also releases", so I left that as documented

items.claim: `usePublishPointer` keeps a stale position after a release off the window that the document never sees
A composed layer's hit drops the region's `hitKind`, so the `docs/extending.md` example's `handle:` predicate never matches
items.note: The defect was the example: `AffordanceRegion.hitKind` already documents that inside a consumer-registered layer the layer id is the discriminator, so the example now matches `layer:my-tool-overlay` and reads the corner from `payload`. Docs only, so no test or changeset; `cornerResize.test.ts` already checks that the scratch reaches the hit

items.claim: `useKeyState({ target })` never attaches if the element mounts after the first effect
`usePublishPointer` reads its element ref once at mount, the same mistake as `useKeyState`
items.note: through a shared `useAttach` helper that re-resolves the element after every commit without an extra render

items.claim: Paint drew regions whose `chromeId` was hidden
items.note: Paint and hit-test now share one `regionShown` check.

items.claim: Annulus paint centered the inner cutout on (cx, cy) while the hit-test used innerX/innerY
items.note: The paint and the `minBandPx` floor now use the rect's real edges.

items.claim: Regions were ranked by world distance under non-uniform zoom
items.note: The ranking now uses screen distance, the same space the hit squares are tested in.
Tool keys and Escape now share one eligibility check.

items.claim: `useKeyState({ target })` never attached to an element that mounted late or was swapped
items.note: A shared core-internal `useElementEffect` re-reads the ref after every render.

items.claim: Middle-drag pan didn't work with a modifier held
items.note: with `mods: ANY_MODS`. The other half, "barred over exclusive chrome", is not a defect: `claimGestureOf` in `packages/routing/src/interactions/dispatcher/matcher.ts:94` makes an exclusive claim cover only the primary press ("a middle drag pans over a handle"). I added a test that holds this; it passes with and without `THROUGH_CHROME`, so `target` was left unset.

The four caps were traced in opposite directions, so where a rect corner fell inside the ellipse (a large `minBandPx`), two overlapping caps cancelled under nonzero fill. The corner could be hit but was not painted. All caps are now traced the same way.

items.claim: `usePublishPointer` read its ref once, the same mistake as `useKeyState` (no reviewer)
items.note: with its own changeset and test. The test fails on the old code.

items.claim: `tool.offhand` (held-key engagement) may skip the mode gate as Escape did (no reviewer)
items.note: question, unverified. `packages/routing/src/interactions/actions/toolOffhand.ts:73` pushes the tool id with no `eligibleForMode` check. It is in `routing`, outside this area, so I left it alone.
